cards.explanation: The answer is on the holy mountains, friends. The song says, "He has founded His city on the holy mountains." Notice who does the founding: He does. The city's foundation is His doing. That's a city built by the best builder there is.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, "The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob." Zion's gates come out on top. And look at the word "loves." The song is talking about love, not just a building.

The word is glorious, friends. "Glorious things are ascribed to you, O city of God." The song turns and talks right to the city, like a friend leaning over to say something good about you. Then the verse ends with "Selah."

The answer is True, friends. The voice says, "I will mention Rahab and Babylon among those who know Me—along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush…" That's a list of names from outside Israel, and the voice counts them among those who know Him. Rahab here is not the Rahab of Jericho, so don't mix those two up.

The answer is "This one was born in Zion," friends, and this is the big moment of the song. The voice mentions Rahab and Babylon, along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush, and says, "This one was born in Zion." Those are names from outside Israel. I'd love to see the faces in the crowd when they hear it.
The answer is the Most High Himself, friends. "…the Most High Himself will establish her." Zion doesn't hold herself up. The Most High does the establishing, personally. That's one steady foundation.

The word is register, friends. The verse says, "The LORD will record in the register of the peoples: 'This one was born in Zion.'" A register is an official list, and the LORD is the one who records in it. Then the verse ends with "Selah," like verse 3 did.

The answer is singers and pipers, friends. The verse says, "Singers and pipers will proclaim…" and then, "All my springs of joy are in You." Voices and pipes, together. I think a song about a city this glad should end with music.
